title: Do emulated quantum circuits change what CNNs look at? Performance and explainability comparison in medical image classification
authors: Guillermo Rubiños Rodríguez, Martín Ottavianelli, Mateo Alonso, Gonzalo Blázquez Gil, Boris-Stephan Rauchmann, Pablo Díez-Valle, Sergio Altares-López
abstract: Numerous studies have analyzed the use of hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural networks as a promising alternative to classical deep learning. However, network components on quantum hardware impose fundamental limitations, while the scalability of quantum circuits leads to trainability issues. In this work, we investigate whether small, classically-emulated quantum circuit components can play a meaningful role within complex models, offering an alternative to purely classical convolutional architectures. To this end, we present a systematic study of the effectiveness of a Hybrid Quantum-inspired Convolutional Neural Network (HQiCNN) compared with a parameter-matched classical Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that differs only in an intermediate dense neural layer. Both models are evaluated on two real-world medical datasets while systematically varying the different hyperparameters, ensuring a fair model comparison that is both dataset and hyperparameter independent. The results show that no architecture consistently dominates the other: the HQiCNN achieves its largest gains in intermediate-data regimes, whereas the CNN reaches the highest accuracies for the largest training sets in both datasets. Furthermore, removing entanglement produces comparable performance while enabling substantially better scalability of quantum simulations, and richer observable sets become beneficial only when sufficient training data are available. Finally, we propose two SHAP-based explainability tools for comparing the predictions between both models, $|SHAP|$IoU and $EMD_{pos}$ metric, to demonstrate that both architectures consistently attend to anatomically plausible regions. Thus, we provide a comprehensive benchmark showing that, under certain conditions, hybrid quantum-inspired models are an alternative that can offer benefits in practical tasks such as medical image classification.
summary: This work compares hybrid quantum-inspired CNNs (HQiCNN) against standard CNNs for medical image classification using emulated quantum circuits. The study finds that performance depends heavily on data availability and hyperparameters, demonstrating that both models can achieve high accuracy while providing comparable, anatomically plausible explanations of their predictions.
main_problem: The study investigates whether small, classically-emulated quantum circuit components can meaningfully enhance complex deep learning models for medical image classification compared to purely classical architectures.
main_result: No single architecture consistently dominates; HQiCNN shows gains in intermediate data regimes, while CNN excels with large datasets. Both methods prove capable of attending to anatomically plausible regions.
method: A systematic comparison was conducted between a Hybrid Quantum-inspired CNN (HQiCNN) and a classical CNN by varying hyperparameters like dataset size, entanglement, and observable sets.
model_or_system: The model uses an emulated quantum circuit component (EQC) with four qubits, parameterized by rotations ($R_X, R_Y, R_Z$) and CNOT gates, which replaces a dense layer in the CNN backbone. This approach avoids physical hardware limitations.
key_observables: $|SHAP|$IoU and $EMD_{pos}$ metrics are used to quantify the spatial overlap and similarity of model attention maps across different architectures and data regimes.
important_parameters: Training set size (1000 vs. 30,000 samples), learning rate ($10^{-2}$ to $10^{-4}$), circuit entanglement status, and observable sets ($	ext{O}1, 	ext{O}2, 	ext{O}3$).
main_assumptions: The quantum component is simulated using native PyTorch functions; the analysis relies on comparing performance under controlled hyperparameter variations.
figures_summary: Figure 6 compares explainability plots ($|SHAP|$IoU) for OCT data across different training sizes, showing consistent attention regions. Figure 6b relates image count to $EMD_{pos}$, demonstrating convergence of explanations with more data.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the HQiCNN vs. CNN comparison, details the model architecture and hyperparameter search space (Table 1), presents results on performance across varying datasets/hyperparameters, and concludes with an explainability analysis using SHAP metrics.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous benchmark for quantum-inspired machine learning models by comparing them against classical baselines under controlled conditions, addressing the question of genuine quantum advantage in practical AI tasks.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
